title: unified-rollouts: proactive shadow canary auto-rollback enhancements
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production rollouts for model changes need earlier, safer detection of regressions while keeping user-facing latency and cost stable. This PR introduces proactive shadow probing and enhanced auto-rollback logic to catch functional and quality regressions before a full traffic migration. Summary: add a staged shadow probing controller, multi-metric rollback decision engine, safety guards (min-samples, cooldown windows, and absolute metric floors), and observability improvements (new Prometheus metrics + Grafana dashboards). Also includes e2e stability tests and docs. Key changes: 1) staged shadow probing pipeline that gradually increases shadow sample rates and probes variants with synthetic and live traffic, 2) multi-metric threshold engine that supports composite rules (latency, token-error-rate, rerank divergence, distributional drift), 3) proactive rollback triggers that can abort or pause rollouts before canary completion when composite thresholds breach, 4) safety guards: min-sample-count, cool-down windows, required confirmatory checks (secondary metric agreement), and forced manual confirmation for model label "critical" rollouts, 5) enhanced observability: per-rollout Prometheus labels, rollout-level tracing spans, and a Grafana dashboard + alert rules, 6) added e2e tests that exercise staged shadow probing under noisy baselines and a migration doc for operators. Backwards compatibility: the default rollout behavior is unchanged unless the new "proactive_shadow" policy is enabled; rollout configs remain compatible. Testing: unit tests for controller logic, integration tests for decision engine, e2e scenarios that simulate latency and semantic regressions, and manual validation in staging with canary traffic. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature-flagged rollout in staging for 48h, run smoke e2e and perf canary, then enable in limited production for 72h under ops monitoring. Related: ENG-2145 (rollout safety), ENG-2210 (observability for rollouts), SUP-342 (customer incident that motivated early detection). Checklist: - [x] Controller and decision engine implemented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] e2e stability tests added - [x] Grafana dashboard and alerts defined - [x] Docs and migration notes updated

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Nice work. Can we add a hard cap on shadow sampling to avoid cost spikes?
Maya Chen: Added a global shadow-sample-cap config and a per-rollout override with sane defaults (see controller.go).
Priya Shah: The multi-metric engine looks good but the default thresholds may be too tight for noisy workloads. Suggest adding a per-workload baseline calibration step.
Maya Chen: Added baseline calibration hook and updated docs to recommend running the calibrator during rollout creation. Defaults loosened and notes added.
Ethan Park: e2e failed on first run due to flakiness in synthetic latency injection. After adjusting timing and retries tests are stable. Marking as flake resolved.
Sara Liu: Approving pending CI green and an additional perf canary run in staging.
